data.name: Avraham
data.gender_notes: Avraham is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avraham is a Hebrew name that translates to 'father of many'. In the Hebrew Bible, Avraham is considered the father of the Jewish people. Avraham's unwavering faith and obedience to God set an example for believers throughout history. The name Avraham carries the meaning “Father of many” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Avraham usually hope their child will grow to embody father of many and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and unwavering obedience to God.
data.etymology: Avraham belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of many.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avraham total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.
data.cultural_impact: Avraham is a significant cultural figure in Judaism and Christianity. In Jewish tradition, he is regarded as the founding patriarch of the Jewish people and the ancestor of the twelve tribes of Israel. In Christianity, Avraham is considered the father of faith and a model of obedience and devotion to God.
data.spiritual_significance: For Jews, Avraham represents the godly patriarch who embodied the qualities of faith and obedience to God's call. For Christians, Avraham is considered a model of faith and an ancestor of the Christian faith. In both traditions, Avraham's unwavering faith and his covenant with God serve as powerful spiritual examples and symbols of the eternal bond between God and His people.
